name: Agrarianism
summary: Agrarianism holds that rural life centred on independent family farms is the best basis for a free and virtuous society. It favours widespread small property, decentralised local self-government and republican politics, and distrusts industry, finance, cities and dependent wage labour. It spans left and right, from Jeffersonian and Southern Agrarian traditionalism to agrarian socialism and Nordic centrist farmers' parties.
scope: The core Anglo-American tradition, taken from Jefferson's Notes on the State of Virginia and the Southern Agrarians of I'll Take My Stand (1930), with the general features documented for agrarian parties and movements. Physiocracy, Maoism and Zapatismo are noted as variants but not the basis. Many answers on modern issues are inferred with low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Agrarian movements never addressed it; Nordic agrarian-descended parties accept welfare states while Jeffersonians and Southern Agrarians distrust central provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Agrarianism centres on independent owners rather than wage labour, so wage law is peripheral and adherents are split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Jeffersonians and Southern Agrarians distrusted commerce, finance and business as eroding independence, though Physiocrats favoured free trade in grain.

public-ownership.rationale: Decentralist and ownership-minded, agrarians prefer many small private owners to state ownership, with agrarian-socialist strands as the exception.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Jefferson proposed a graduated income tax to discourage concentrations of wealth, and agrarian parties defend small farmers against the powerful.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are not a core agrarian topic; agrarians value independence over wage employment, but agrarian-left strands back organised labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: Widespread ownership is central, so property is valued, though agrarians accept redistribution and limits on large holdings.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Distrust of industrial and financial concentrations that undermine independent producers suggests support for restraining them.

cut-welfare.rationale: Agrarians prize self-reliance, but agrarian-rooted parties in the Nordic countries support welfare, so adherents are split.

worker-ownership.rationale: Agrarian support for cooperatives and broad ownership extends naturally to worker-owned businesses, inferred from the property principle.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Inferred from republican distrust of concentrated state power and emphasis on local self-government.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed; rural conservative and decentralist strands pull in opposite directions.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Inferred from republican suspicion of central authority; not addressed directly.

strong-leader.rationale: Agrarians favoured republicanism over monarchy and aristocracy, so a leader bypassing legislatures is disfavoured.

state-harmful.rationale: Agrarianism wants decentralised, limited government, not abolition of the state.

limit-guns.rationale: Inferred from rural, self-reliant culture of armed independent farmers; not stated in sources.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; agrarian tradition suspects standing power but rural conservatives favour order.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the traditional, family-centred values of rural agrarian society.

decide-locally.rationale: Political decentralisation and local self-government are core agrarian principles.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by agrarian sources and adherents likely split.

traditional-family.rationale: Agrarianism values family farming and stable family and regional ties.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, family-centred outlook of mainstream agrarianism; not addressed directly.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the religious and family-centred outlook; not addressed directly.

more-religion-public.rationale: Southern Agrarians prized regional religiosity and agrarians see farming as nearer to God; policy on public religion is inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Strands diverge sharply, with some agrarians defending the Old South and others like Warren supporting civil rights.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from traditional family values; not addressed.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Southern Agrarians sought to preserve regional tradition and agrarians prefer local tradition to urban modernity.

gradual-change.rationale: Agrarians prefer settled traditional community life, so gradual change is inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Inferred from decentralist and local-sovereignty orientation.

free-trade.rationale: Physiocrat du Pont advocated free trade, while Jefferson supported tariffs for revenue, so the tradition is split.

nation-first.rationale: Not central; Jefferson wanted to trade farm goods for European manufactures but agrarians show no consistent line.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Inferred from the localist, inward-looking outlook.

open-borders.rationale: Inferred from attachment to local and regional community; not addressed.

limit-growth.rationale: Later agrarians such as Berry and Leopold stress ecology and simple living, though earlier agrarians did not address growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Not addressed; environmental agrarians favour action but farm-defending parties split.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Agrarians hold that technology erodes independence and dignity and fosters weakness.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from distrust of industrial technology and large centralised systems.

revolution-justified.rationale: Zapatista and Maoist strands say yes while Jeffersonian and Southern strands favour settled order.

experts-over-public.rationale: Inferred from republican confidence in independent citizen-farmers and suspicion of urban elites.

central-planning.rationale: Mainstream agrarians favour independent family farms and decentralisation; Maoist collectivisation is a minority strand.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between private family farms and cooperative or agrarian-socialist models.

land-value-tax.rationale: Physiocrats saw land as the source of wealth and Jefferson wanted to curb concentrated holdings; the specific tax is inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Jefferson's wish to discourage concentrations of wealth.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Jefferson used tariffs for revenue and agrarians prefer farming to industry, so protecting industry is not a clear agrarian aim.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Inferred from decentralist preference for independent local producers.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Widespread ownership and family farming are central goals of agrarianism.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Agrarians disparage wage dependence but aim at independent owners, not abolishing money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Jeffersonians saw financiers and banks as centres of corruption; abolition itself is inferred.

one-party-rule.rationale: Agrarians favoured republican government, and Southern Agrarians opposed communism and fascism.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Agrarians favoured republicanism over monarchy and aristocracy.

democracy-best.rationale: Agrarians wanted independent voters who could not be swayed by employers, a democratic republican ideal.

direct-votes.rationale: Local self-government and village-level decision-making are emphasised; wider direct legislation is inferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Not an agrarian form; agrarians centre on farmers and local community.

right-to-secede.rationale: Inferred from decentralist principles and Southern Agrarian regionalism.

political-violence-never.rationale: Not stated; agrarian strands include revolutionaries, so never is too strong.

war-builds-character.rationale: Agrarians credit farm labour, not war, with building virtue.

separate-church-state.rationale: Jefferson favoured separation while Southern Agrarians prized religiosity, so adherents are split.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Agrarians link farming to piety but have no program for scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from republican, community-based government rather than privatised law.

military-superiority.rationale: Inferred from localist, non-expansionist rural outlook.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Not part of agrarian doctrine; agrarian parties organise around class and region.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Mainstream agrarians defend small farmers against elites but do not make class conflict history's engine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Agrarians seek broad property ownership, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Zapatistas stress collective land ownership while mainstream agrarians do not address it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

civilizational-union.rationale: Inferred from localist preference for small communities.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Agrarians stress community, honor and moral integrity over self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Agrarians value community but also independence; adherents are split.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Later agrarians such as Berry and Leopold value nature in itself, and agrarians see farming as tied to God's order.

limit-population.rationale: Inferred from family-centred values; not addressed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Agrarians hold industrialism erodes independence and community, though few use the word disaster.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technology and industrialism are blamed for eroding independence and dignity.

human-enhancement.rationale: Inferred from distrust of technology and attachment to natural life.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inferred from distrust of technology and preference for local self-rule.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

restore-past-order.rationale: Southern Agrarians looked back to an older order but Jeffersonians aimed at a republic of independent farmers going forward.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

direct-action.rationale: Mainstream agrarianism works through parties and republican institutions.

means-match-ends.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Agrarians exalt cultivation of the soil, not hunter-gathering.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Southern Agrarians kept room for professions and arts; only the ancient Chinese Agriculturalists approached this.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

production-for-use.rationale: Self-sufficient family farming implies producing for subsistence and community more than for profit, an inference.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Agrarian socialists and Physiocrats criticise profit but mainstream agrarians do not use this theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Alien to the republican mainstream of agrarianism.

collective-farming.rationale: Family farming is central, and Maoist collectivisation led to famine and is a minority strand.

taxation-theft.rationale: Agrarians accept taxation, as Jefferson's tariffs and graduated income tax show.

harm-principle.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Agrarians value both individual independence and community.

conscription.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Agrarians favour democracy and rooted community over exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Agrarians distrust business and finance as models.

positive-liberty.rationale: Jefferson held that dependence breeds subservience, so independence requires holding means of livelihood; stated in terms of property.

media-academia-power.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

organic-representation.rationale: Local community and village-level decision-making are emphasised; representation by bodies is inferred.

total-state.rationale: Agrarianism is decentralist and Southern Agrarians opposed communism and fascism.

national-rebirth.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

bound-labor.rationale: Agrarians prize independent farmers who own land, the opposite of bound labour.

universal-morality.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Inferred from Jeffersonian suspicion of finance and banks.

rule-by-example.rationale: Agrarians prize virtue but not as a mode of government.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Agrarians link farming to religion and tradition.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Inferred from agrarian praise of labour and self-reliance.

ban-interest.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not stated; mainstream agrarianism does not centre race.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Agrarian republicanism rests on citizens' equality before a republic, though Jefferson and Southern Agrarians tolerated racial hierarchy.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Jeffersonian republicanism rests on consent of independent citizens.

trade-surplus.rationale: Physiocrats criticised mercantilism, which pursued trade surpluses.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are split between pacifist and rural self-defence traditions.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Agrarians stress cooperation in the farming community.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Jefferson argued that dependence begets subservience, the republican idea of freedom as independence.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Agrarian parties aim to protect small farmers and poor peasants against wealthier groups.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Agrarians blame concentration of land and wealth, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Inferred from republican limits on power.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Farmers benefit from higher prices, so adherents would be split.

party-controls-media.rationale: Inferred from republican and decentralist outlook.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Inferred from republican wariness of executive power.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

clerical-rule.rationale: Agrarians value religion but favour republican government.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Southern Agrarians valued arts and scholarship in agrarian society.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Inferred from Jeffersonian opposition to entrenched executive power.

recall-officials.rationale: Inferred from local self-government and anti-elite orientation.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Inferred from localist outlook; not addressed in opened sources.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Widespread ownership is sought, but an outright ban on renting goes beyond it.

people-in-arms.rationale: Agrarian sources do not address this question, and adherents would likely be split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Jefferson called those who labour in the earth the chosen people of God and said city mobs support government as sores do the body; agrarianism generally holds farming builds virtue.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Agrarian traditions did not address partition; nationalist and decentralist strands pull in different directions.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Jefferson prized the independent cultivator, and Southern Agrarians attacked abstract, industrial modernity and its intellectuals; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Southern Agrarians defended their own traditional regional culture as superior to industrial modernity; inferred, and adherents vary.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; traditionalist strands tend to support it while agrarian socialists and Nordic centrists oppose it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Traditionalist agrarianism places moral upbringing with family and community; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Rural religious communities often favour it, but agrarian movements as a whole never took a position; split.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Traditional rural moral outlook favours legal restriction of obscenity; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed in agrarian texts; Jefferson's republic welcomed settlers while rooted-community strands favour descent.

minority-language-support.rationale: Agrarian parties in minority regions support it while Anglo-American strands never raised it; split.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not addressed; republican equality before the law and rural religious sympathy pull in opposite ways.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Southern Agrarians valued inherited custom and settled community over individual experiment; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from agrarian distrust of finance and creditors, which in agrarian movements usually favoured relief for indebted farmers, extended here to poor countries.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the agrarian view that real independence rests on widely held land, as in Jefferson's argument that dependence breeds subservience.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Inferred from agrarianism's republican and locally self-governing politics, which favour constitutions made by elected popular bodies; not a defining issue.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Inferred from agrarian republican commitment to liberty and its suspicion of forced industrial development.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition's localism and wariness of centralised provision pull against a global duty, while its moral emphasis on stewardship and small producers pulls toward it.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as split between the tradition's distrust of standing military power and its nationalist strands.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Inferred from the republican, popular-sovereignty strain of agrarian politics; it is not a defining issue.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Inferred from agrarian hostility to banks and finance, which Jefferson's followers directed against a national bank and later agrarian populists against monetary elites.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed; agrarian attachment to the land is strong but the tradition has no position on territorial settlements.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Agrarians defend private property chiefly as widely distributed family holdings that sustain independence and civic virtue, which implies a social purpose; inferred rather than stated.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Agrarian traditions oppose communism, but they have not taken a stand on the state-capitalist label, and agrarian socialists differ on it.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Stewardship of land is a recurring agrarian theme, so caution about environmental harm is inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Agrarians are wary of foreign entanglements and distant government (the audit records end-foreign-alliances as +1); inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Agrarianism has no recorded position on annexation, and adherents split; inferred.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Agrarians prize local, traditional institutions including religion against central power; inferred.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Jefferson was himself a partisan leader and agrarian parties are party-based, so this is split; inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The audit records a lean toward a right to secede, and Southern Agrarians defended Southern self-determination; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Southern Agrarian regionalism and decentralised local self-government favour regions keeping their own ways.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Jefferson was a republican who rejected hereditary and sacral kingship; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Agrarians distrust finance and concentrated wealth and the audit records support for taxing the wealthy; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Jefferson holds that working the land produces virtue, treating circumstances as the source of character; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Agrarian republicanism holds that rulers answer to the people and law, as Jefferson did; inferred.

space-expansion.rationale: Agrarians distrust technological progress and favour rooted rural life over expansion; inferred.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Jefferson favoured a broadly democratic republic with separated powers, not an explicit mix of few and many; inferred as split.

leader-cult.rationale: Republican simplicity and distrust of concentrated power make public glorification of a leader alien to agrarians; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Agrarianism says nothing about custody, and traditional-family views pull against modern shared-parenting presumptions; inferred as split.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Southern Agrarians opposed communism and Jeffersonians prized independent proprietors, though agrarian socialists differ; inferred as a mild no.

land-redistribution.rationale: Widespread small family-farm ownership is a core agrarian aim, and agrarian parties have backed breaking up large estates.

refugee-return.rationale: Agrarian thought never addressed refugee return and strands differ; left neutral as an inference.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Agrarianism centers on local attachment to land, not expansion on grounds of nationality; inferred.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Agrarians generally favor tradition but Jeffersonian republicanism backs freedom of conscience; inferred as a mild no.

women-must-cover.rationale: Agrarians are traditional on family and religion, but a legal covering requirement was never an agrarian demand; inferred.

common-currency.rationale: Agrarianism distrusts finance and centralized institutions in favor of local self-government; inferred.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Agrarianism centers on local rootedness rather than cross-border political unions; inferred.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Decentralization and local self-government are core agrarian themes, so autonomous local institutions fit; inferred.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Agrarians value rootedness in the land where one lives, so building a life and claiming rights at home fits; inferred.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Southern Agrarians stress tradition, religion and culture against industrial materialism; inferred as a mild no.

ban-cartels.rationale: Agrarians distrust concentrated industry and finance and prefer widespread small property; inferred that they favor breaking up cartels.

no-bailouts.rationale: Agrarians distrust finance, but farmers' parties often support state aid in crises; adherents are split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Jefferson feared unchecked power in any branch and Nordic agrarians accept constitutional rules; adherents are split.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Traditionalist agrarians do not make equal representation by sex a goal, though agrarian-descended Nordic parties accept it; inferred.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Agrarianism prizes self-reliant farm communities and Jefferson favored farming over foreign manufactures; inferred as a mild yes.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Agrarian parties differ on trade, with farm lobbies split on binding standards; inferred as split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Agrarians prize virtue and duty but also independence and property; adherents are split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Agrarian republicanism favors lawful self-government and Southern Agrarians opposed revolutionary movements; inferred.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Jefferson's republicanism and a society of independent farmers oppose inherited aristocracy; inferred as a mild yes.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Southern Agrarians prized tradition and regional rootedness, which suggests teaching the home tradition first; inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Jeffersonian republicanism stresses self-government and independence, which cuts against rule over other peoples; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Agrarians value local tradition and republican virtue, which suggests civic and patriotic schooling; inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Agrarianism spans left and right and its Southern wing split over segregation, so adherents divide on race-conscious policy.

public-money-creation.rationale: Agrarian traditions distrust banks and finance, and populist agrarians sought public control of credit; inferred.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Agrarians opposed industrialism as ruinous and expected it to undermine society, which leans toward doubting capitalism's durability; inferred.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Agrarianism favours decentralised, local self-government and wariness of empire; inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: Agrarians prefer local self-sufficiency over manufactures and trade, but Nordic farmers' parties accepted open trade; adherents split.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Agrarianism prizes self-sufficiency of farm and community; inferred it extends to national development.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not addressed; agrarian parties range from isolationist to nationalist.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred: the Jeffersonian and Southern traditions rest on settler yeoman farmers and do not support descent-based leadership.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Southern Agrarians opposed fascism and communism alike, but agrarians have no stance on constitutional founding values.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Southern Agrarians opposed both communism and fascism as threats to tradition and independence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Southern Agrarians tended to Lost Cause views, while Jeffersonian and other strands do not; the tradition is split.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Traditionalist, rooted agrarians favour preserving inherited symbols; inferred from reverence for tradition.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as split between traditionalist and left agrarian strands.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Not addressed by agrarian writers; inferred as split.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Agrarians favour institutions shaped by local tradition and place over imported universal models.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Jefferson distrusted standing armies and favoured citizen militias under civil control.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred: the family farm treats household labour as part of shared family economy, not as wage labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Agrarian thought centres on the multigenerational family farm and traditional family ties, so lifelong duty to parents is inferred as fitting.

office-by-exam.rationale: Jeffersonian agrarians trusted locally chosen officials and rural self-government over a credentialed bureaucracy; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Agrarians distrust finance and distant concentrated capital, so keeping strategic firms in national hands is inferred as acceptable.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Southern Agrarians defended traditional social order and family, so easy dissolution of marriage is inferred as disfavoured.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Agrarians favour small-scale, local, accountable republican government, so binding and recallable representatives is inferred as fitting.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Agrarian movements never addressed pension design; Jeffersonians favour individual self-reliance while agrarian-descended parties accept state pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Agrarians favour owner-cultivators holding land outright, though agrarian socialists favour common tenure; inferred as disagree for the mainstream.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Jeffersonian republicanism holds that the people's representatives control the public purse; inferred from agrarian republican politics.

single-official-language.rationale: Agrarian movements did not address official-language policy; rural and minority farmers' parties differ.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Agrarians prize land held by the native cultivators of a country, and farmland ownership by outsiders is a common agrarian worry; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Agrarian traditionalists such as the Southern Agrarians stress intent and individual responsibility over group-outcome tests; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: I'll Take My Stand opposes industrial consumption and the cult of material progress, and Jefferson prefers frugal farm life over luxury.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Agrarian republicans distrust foreign entanglement and standing military power, so arming foreign rebels is inferred as disfavoured.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Agrarianism is inward-looking and local, and its republican tradition opposes imperial force; inferred.

corporate-influence.rationale: Agrarians distrust finance and industry and favour independent small owners; corporate power over government follows from this.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Agrarian localism and distrust of finance suggest wariness of outside funding; inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Southern Agrarians defended family and rural community life, so support for family-building policy is inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Agrarians prize rooted local self-government and land held by those who work it; limiting purchases to residents is inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Agrarians favour independent proprietors over dependent wage labour and are wary of central programmes; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Jeffersonian republicanism favours self-government but Agrarians never made peace through democracy a theme; split.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Jefferson held that legitimate government rests on consent, and Agrarians prize local liberty over state authority; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Jeffersonian tradition favours avoiding entanglements with other nations; inferred as support for non-intervention.

industrial-unions.rationale: Agrarians distrust industry and wage labour but did not address unions; left neutral.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Agrarianism has no doctrine of minority conspiracy; it is not central, though some Southern Agrarians shared regional prejudices.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: I'll Take My Stand defends the traditional family and religion as part of the rooted agrarian order.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Jefferson held that self-government needs an informed citizenry; a legal right of access is inferred.

local-production.rationale: Agrarianism holds that communities should live from their own land and distrusts the industrial economy.

informal-organisation.rationale: Agrarian movements organised through grange-style societies and parties, and favour local government; informal-only organisation is not their model.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Agrarians' localism and Jeffersonian suspicion of distant authority favour national and local law over foreign bodies; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: Southern Agrarians defended religion as part of rural life but Jefferson favoured separation; adherents split.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Inferred: Jeffersonian agrarians favoured avoiding entangling foreign relations, and the variant sources do not support ritual submission to a power.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from agrarian support for decentralised local self-government, though farm-based parties often accept transfers to rural regions, so adherents are split.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Agrarianism rests on widespread private ownership of land by family farmers and the Southern Agrarians opposed communism.

defeat-communism.rationale: The Southern Agrarians opposed communism along with industrialism, but agrarian socialists dissent, so the strands are split.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Agrarian traditions split on public services, with Nordic agrarian parties accepting welfare states and Jeffersonians distrusting central provision.

religion-illusion.rationale: The Southern Agrarians' Statement of Principles defends religious tradition against the industrial mind, and Jefferson's farmers are cast as a virtuous chosen people.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Jefferson and the Agrarians distrust industry and finance and hold that dependent wage labour undermines independence.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred: traditionalist agrarians defended inherited family roles, while agrarian-socialist variants would differ.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred: the family farm household is the basic unit of agrarian life, and nothing in the sources endorses public provision of domestic work.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Inferred: agrarian traditionalists value local culture but the sources do not address language purism, so this is weakly negative.

treaties-binding.rationale: Not addressed in the sources, and Jefferson's land policy toward Native nations points in different directions from other agrarian movements.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Agrarianism favours independent family farms held as private property, not communal ownership, though some agrarian-socialist strands differ.

majority-settlement.rationale: Agrarian settlement of farmland was not ethnically targeted in the sources, so adherents are not clearly for or against this.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The Southern Agrarians opposed both industrial capitalism and communism, offering a rural third course.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Agrarians prized rootedness and attachment to place, but ties of whole peoples to territory were not their concern; inferred only, adherents would be split.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Never addressed; a typical adherent of this republican, moral-order tradition would accept the historical record, inferred from its general respect for truth and civic virtue.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not addressed by Jefferson or the Southern Agrarians as a programme; the traditionalist strand leans to criminalisation while modern Nordic and agrarian-socialist strands do not.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Agrarianism is republican and favours decentralised self-government by independent citizens, which is incompatible with suppressing opposition for order.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Jefferson's republicanism leaned to civil freedom in religion, though Southern Agrarians were pro-religion; inferred, not stated in the sources.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Agrarian ideals centre on self-governing independent farmers, so ruling dependent territories for the metropole's profit is inferred to be foreign to it.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A specifically Islamic religious duty on which agrarianism has no position; adherents would be indifferent.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The republican tradition holds that rulers' legitimacy rests on consent, not religious law, and does not endorse forcible removal on religious grounds; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Decentralised local self-government by independent proprietors is a core agrarian aim, and distant officialdom is distrusted.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; the core tradition is organised around independent owners versus dependency rather than overlapping identity oppressions, so inferred disagreement.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not addressed; the traditionalist core of the tradition (Southern Agrarians) is socially conservative, inferred at low confidence.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the traditional, religiously inflected outlook of the core tradition.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Agrarianism spans left and right, from Southern Agrarian traditionalism to agrarian socialism and Nordic centrist parties, so adherents readily mix elements of each; inferred.

alienated-labor.rationale: I'll Take My Stand argues industrial labour deprives workers of satisfaction in work that farming provides, and Jefferson condemned dependent wage labour.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; adherents would be split along their wider cultural conservatism.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Jefferson grounded government in the consent of the governed and Southern Agrarians were religious but not theocratic; inferred.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not addressed; republican separation of church and state and traditional religiosity pull in opposite directions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern employment-law issue peripheral to agrarianism, which centres on independent owners rather than wage labour; adherents split.

social-market-economy.rationale: Nordic agrarian-descended parties accept welfare capitalism while Jeffersonians and Southern Agrarians distrust both industry and central provision.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Jefferson distrusted standing armies but relied on citizen militias for defence; inferred rejection of abolishing armed forces outright.

rich-first.rationale: Agrarianism favours widespread small property and distrusts concentrated wealth and finance, so letting some grow rich first runs against it.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Jefferson's republic of farmers is generally associated with avoiding foreign entanglements; inferred, not drawn from the cited texts.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Agrarianism is republican and rests on independent citizen-farmers, so hereditary office sits badly with it.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Inferred from agrarian distrust of finance and the farmer cooperatives and credit unions of agrarian movements; credit was not a defining theme of the Jeffersonian or Southern strands.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from agrarian hostility to banks and creditors holding farmers in debt; modern lender conditions were not addressed.

property-franchise.rationale: Jefferson favoured freeholder suffrage in his early drafts while later agrarians backed broad farmer enfranchisement, so adherents are split.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Agrarians prize stewardship of the land but the Southern strand upheld traditional gender roles; the ecofeminist claim was not addressed.

reification.rationale: Inferred from the Southern Agrarian critique of industrial and commercial life that turns persons and labour into commodities.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from agrarian distrust of concentrated wealth and its influence; press ownership was not discussed.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the republican preference for government under known laws; not stated in the sources.

racial-franchise.rationale: Jefferson's republic included only free citizens and the Southern Agrarians defended segregation, but agrarian parties generally did not make race the basis of the vote; inferred and contested.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; local self-government favours face-to-face deliberation while agrarians distrust technology, and modern agrarian parties accept it.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the republican and decentralised preference for accountable, locally visible government.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from agrarian rural communitarianism that was often religiously homogeneous, though marriage law was not addressed; contested.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred; agrarian movements did not promote boycotts of minority-owned shops as a policy, and Jefferson defended religious liberty.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Jefferson favoured small self-governing local wards where ordinary citizens decide public business directly, but sortition itself was never proposed; inferred from that participatory localism.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The Southern Agrarians defended traditional religion against modern scientific rationalism; inferred from that stance, since reinterpreting doctrine was not their theme.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Jefferson held that dependence corrupts virtue and that widespread small property underlies republican liberty; agrarians distrust concentrated finance and landholding.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Anachronistic; traditionalist Southern Agrarians would likely disagree while agrarian-descended Nordic centrist parties are mixed, so inferred mildly negative.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Southern Agrarians defended religion and tradition against industrial secularism, and Jefferson favoured religious freedom, so state atheism is alien to the tradition.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Agrarians favour local self-government and community order but never called for abolishing police; inferred as opposed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; agrarianism favours decentralised local government, and adherents are split on consociational arrangements.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Agrarians favour self-reliant local communities, but agrarian parties also accepted state farm support, so the strands differ.

term-limits.rationale: Jefferson supported rotation in office and distrust of entrenched power, but term limits were not an agrarian programme; inferred mildly positive.

vote-delegation.rationale: Anachronistic; agrarians favour direct local participation but the idea is not part of the tradition.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; agrarians' stress on stewardship of land does not translate into a stance on extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Southern Agrarians were religiously and socially traditionalist, and Nordic agrarian parties moderate; inferred mildly opposed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Southern Agrarians defended traditional family and gender roles, so husband-led authority is inferred as the typical view, though not stated in the sources.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Inferred: agrarian politics rests on rooted local communities of owners, so voting by non-citizen residents is not favoured.

rent-control.rationale: Agrarians favour owner-farmers, but tenant farmers and landlords divide adherents; inferred as split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Agrarianism never addressed intellectual property; inferred as split.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred: agrarian decentralism and distrust of the state fit poorly with drilled national youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed by agrarians; inferred as split.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Jefferson favoured avoiding foreign entanglements, but agrarians never addressed basing; inferred as split.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; inferred as split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Jefferson praises cultivators who earn from their own labour and distrusts dependence, though agrarians also prize owning land.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred: the rural tradition of independent self-reliant owners values self-defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Southern Agrarians prize inherited tradition, but the strand is split on how far national continuity runs.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist outlook of the Southern Agrarians.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditional and religious outlook of the core Anglo-American strand.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Not addressed by the tradition; inferred as split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Southern Agrarians defended religion against industrialism, but the tradition does not frame politics as a cosmic struggle.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed by agrarians; inferred as split.

culture-before-state.rationale: Southern Agrarians stressed tradition and culture against industrialism, but also local politics; adherents split.

god-not-male.rationale: Inferred from the religious traditionalism of the Southern Agrarians.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist religion of the core strand.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Not addressed beyond the Southern strand's split on segregation; inferred as split.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed by agrarians; inferred as split.

independent-unions.rationale: Agrarian writing focuses on independent farmers, not unions, so this is inferred as split.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Agrarian socialists would agree while Jeffersonians and Southern Agrarians would not, so adherents split.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Agrarian thought favours local community institutions, so local services staying public is inferred as mildly agreeable.

second-chamber.rationale: Agrarians have no settled view on the structure of legislatures.

municipal-property.rationale: Agrarianism favours widespread private family farms and holds that independent property makes free citizens, so community ownership of production is rejected.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Agrarians prefer decentralised local self-government, so joint bodies that only coordinate are inferred as fitting.

family-wage.rationale: Agrarians centre the family farm and the household, so wages that support a family are inferred as agreeable.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation is outside agrarian concerns, so this is neutral.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Agrarians favour natural rhythms of life and distrust technological ambitions, so large spending on ageing research is inferred as disfavoured.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Agrarians distrust finance, but nothing in their texts addresses payment privacy.

online-anonymity.rationale: Online anonymity is anachronistic, and agrarian principles do not decide it.

person-over-state.rationale: Jefferson's yeoman farmer is independent and self-governing, so the person should not be a mere instrument of the state; inferred.

spiritual-nature.rationale: The Southern Agrarians argued that industrial life impoverishes the spirit and defended religion and the arts against a purely economic way of life.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Agrarians favour decentralised power and states' or local rights, so powers revocable by the national legislature are disfavoured; inferred.

gm-crops.rationale: Agrarians distrust industrial agriculture and favour traditional small-scale farming, so embracing engineered crops is disfavoured by inference.

dense-cities.rationale: Jefferson called great cities sores on the body politic, a claim about public morals; the environmental comparison in the statement is a modern question, so disagreement is inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Agrarianism is organised by occupation and region, not race, though the Southern Agrarians had racial attitudes of their time; inferred.

racial-pride.rationale: Agrarian writers prized inheritance and place, but racial pride is not a stated principle, so adherents split.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Jefferson favoured peace and small armies, and agrarians distrust standing military power, so defence only is inferred.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Agrarianism is about rural life and property, not how a nation is defined; Southern Agrarians were regionalist and adherents have not shared one view.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from the republican, common-citizenship tradition of Jefferson; separate religious electorates are not part of agrarian thought.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Inferred: the tradition is inward-looking and wary of entanglements, but partition plots are not a theme in the sources.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed; Jeffersonians favoured education for citizens but distrusted central provision, and Nordic agrarian parties accept welfare provision.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: agrarians stress stewardship, property and local control and distrust finance, so a market-pricing tax as the main tool is unlikely to be favoured.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from the family-farm ideal of land held and passed down across generations as a trust.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Inferred: the Southern Agrarians defended traditional family and social roles, so giving women's outlook extra weight is unlikely to be endorsed.

arms-reduction.rationale: Inferred from Jeffersonian distrust of standing armies and the Agrarians' hostility to industrial and state power.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from Jefferson's republican distrust of unaccountable government and its secret dealings.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from agrarian distrust of finance and the money power; the sources do not discuss capital flows directly.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the Jeffersonian ideal of independent citizens and a decentralised polity, which favours an armed yeomanry and local militias over a standing state force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred: agrarians prize loyalty to home and region and fought in their countries' wars, though they distrust standing armies and foreign entanglements.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Agrarians distrust dependent wage labour but also industrial unions, and favour farmers' cooperatives; adherents are split.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from Jefferson's view that dependence breeds subservience and the agrarian ideal of self-reliant property owners over state top-ups.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from agrarian distrust of finance and debt, which Jefferson and farmers' parties shared; not set out in the sources as a legal rule.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Agrarian parties want protection for farmers and fair terms of trade, but no single view on world economic rules emerges; inferred as split.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Agrarians were republican reformers and traditionalists who opposed both communist and fascist upheavals and valued inherited local institutions.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Agrarianism favours decentralised local self-government and small property, which allows varied local arrangements, though it has its own ideal of the farming economy; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: I'll Take My Stand objects to industrial exploitation of nature and treats land as a way of life, not an asset to price; inferred.

sacred-nation.rationale: Agrarians prize place and region, and Nordic farmers' parties are often nationalist, but sacralising the nation is not a core agrarian idea; split.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; agrarians are wary of debt and dependence but also of the urban professional class.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Agrarians hold that cities, industry and finance draw wealth from the countryside, as the Southern Agrarians said of industrial interests and as Jefferson said of cities as sores on the body politic.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist strand of agrarianism, which holds that virtue comes from a constant human condition tied to the land and tradition.

public-service-media.rationale: Agrarians distrust concentrated power, public and private alike; the Nordic strand accepted public broadcasting and the US strand did not.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Southern Agrarians defended traditional, rooted (largely Protestant) religion as part of a settled way of life; perennialism is not an agrarian doctrine, so this is inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: Agrarian parties and movements are documented as defending the family farm against markets, creditors and finance, which price supports and cooperative credit serve directly.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Never addressed; Jeffersonian distrust of standing power and Nordic agrarian pacifism pull against rural patriotic security views, so adherents are split.

workers-own-party.rationale: Agrarians organised their own farmers parties and the agrarian-socialist strand allied with labour, but the statement is about workers and the core tradition is not wage labour; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the republican concern for individual bodily independence and the rule of law, with no agrarian doctrine defending the practice.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The tradition prizes widespread small property but historically centred on the male household head; modern agrarian parties accept equal rights, so this is inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed by any agrarian source; a linguistic classification question with no ideological bearing.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Agrarians defend landholders against industrial harm and favour local, decentralised remedies, which fits property-based liability, though they also accept regulation; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Never addressed; the tradition values local rooted authority but is republican and elected, so adherents would be split.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Agrarians prize stewardship of land and distrust industry but equally prize independent landholders free of outside control, so they are split.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Jeffersonian preference for local juries and distrust of centralised state power.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; Southern Agrarian emphasis on a settled shared local culture suggests mild support, while Jefferson welcomed settlers; inferred.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Agrarians centre on independent owners rather than wage labour, and agrarian socialists and conservatives differ, so it is split.

voter-id.rationale: Voter identification is not addressed by the sources, and adherents range from rural conservatives to agrarian socialists, so it is neutral.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Southern Agrarians defended traditional religion while Nordic agrarian parties were secular, so adherents are split.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Jefferson ties republican government to independent landholders, so democracy as electoral procedure alone is inferred as insufficient.

premarital-sex.rationale: Southern Agrarians defended traditional social and family morals, so sex outside marriage for women is inferred as not acceptable.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Agrarians favour decentralised local self-government and distrust central power, so national shutdowns are inferred as disagreeable.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Nordic agrarian-descended parties accept welfare while Jeffersonians distrust central provision, so it is split.

women-suffrage.rationale: Early agrarians such as Jefferson and the Southern Agrarians did not centre suffrage while agrarian parties later accepted it, so it is split.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Agrarians defend traditional religion and family life, so blaming religion for women's oppression is inferred as rejected.

race-social-construct.rationale: Southern Agrarians were divided on segregation and the sources do not discuss race theory, so it is neutral.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Agrarians favour small local government and traditional family roles, so dedicated national agencies are inferred as disagreeable.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Agrarians favoured widespread small freeholds and homestead policy, but Query XIX praises those who labour in the earth and says nothing about original appropriation by first use; mild agreement is inferred.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Inferred from the agrarian preference for local self-government and distrust of distant centralised authority; the question was never addressed.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Southern Agrarians were often religious traditionalists but Jeffersonian agrarians were deists; adherents are split and no source treats literalism.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Agrarianism never addressed Indigenous self-government or gender guarantees; the tradition spans left and right, so this is inferred as split.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Agrarianism distrusts concentrated power, though agrarian socialists differ; defending a bureaucratic planned state is inferred as disliked.

indirect-election.rationale: Jefferson favoured ward republics built from local bodies while agrarian movements also backed direct democracy; this is inferred and split.

national-church-status.rationale: Jefferson opposed established churches, though Southern Agrarians were more traditionalist; the majority view is inferred as against.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Agrarian decentralism favours local self-rule but the tradition never addressed ethnic territorial autonomy, so this is inferred as split.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Not addressed; local self-government points toward a vote but agrarianism has no stated position on territorial disputes.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Agrarianism never addressed decolonisation borders, so this is inferred as neutral.

simple-living.rationale: Agrarianism prizes the self-sufficient family farm, limited wants and distrust of commerce and luxury, as Jefferson and I'll Take My Stand argue.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the Jeffersonian drive to settle western land with yeoman farmers; later agrarian movements were split, so confidence is low.

equal-conscription.rationale: Agrarianism never addressed conscription and Southern traditionalists and agrarian leftists would differ on women serving, so this is inferred as split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Agrarians hold that people rooted in the land are the foundation of virtue; Jefferson calls cultivators God's chosen people and the Southern Agrarians defend a traditional life tied to the soil.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred from republican, law-bound government in Jefferson; the sources do not address drug policy.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic; agrarian parties differ and the tradition gives no guidance on China.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred; agrarian movements range from nationalist to local-minded and the sources do not discuss kin minorities.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Agrarians want land widely held by family farmers, which sits between private ownership and equal claims to land; adherents split.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the agrarian ideal of independent proprietors who answer to no master, as in Jefferson's account of dependence breeding subservience.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred: agrarians favour small producers and householders, and consumption taxes weigh on rural households; the sources give no tax policy.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not addressed; agrarian socialists and Nordic farmers' parties differ on universal versus targeted welfare.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from the agrarian preference for decentralised, direct local self-government over distant organisations.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Agrarians distrust finance and industry and favour wide small property, so special privileges for big business are inferred as opposed.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Jefferson favoured separating church and state, while Southern Agrarians defended religion in public life; adherents split.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Southern Agrarians opposed industrialism and chose the traditional agrarian way of life over it rather than merging the two.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred; traditionalist agrarians would resist while agrarian socialists and Nordic centrists would not, and sources do not address it.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from agrarian suspicion of finance and distant capital and the interest of rural people in control of their land.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Agrarians prize widely held private property earned by one's own labour on the land, which suits a process view of fairness, though Jeffersonians also accepted redistributing land; inferred.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Agrarians distrust finance and speculators; a tax on financial trading follows from that suspicion, though no source states it.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Agrarian movements range from Southern traditionalists who defended segregation to agrarian socialists and farmer-labour movements, so adherents are split.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Jeffersonian republicans cited natural rights against tyrannical law but the Southern Agrarians stressed custom and tradition; adherents are split on this.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Agrarians distrust industrial technology and prize labour on the land as the basis of virtue, so they would resist maximising automation; inferred from that.

multipolar-world.rationale: Agrarians favour decentralised, local self-government and wariness of concentrated power, which extends to many centres over one hegemon; inferred.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Jefferson held that cultivators of the earth are the most valuable citizens and Agrarians privilege labour on the land over finance, though they gave no value theory; inferred.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Agrarian movements tie love of homeland and rural community to the interests of farmers and working producers; inferred from their populist character.

material-over-identity.rationale: Agrarian movements split between farm-economy populists and cultural traditionalists, so there is no single view of left priorities.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Agrarians favour independent small proprietors and local self-government over party-state control; some agrarian socialists dissent, so this is inferred.

missingStatements.text: Rural life is morally healthier than life in cities.
missingStatements.rationale: Jefferson called those who labour in the earth God's chosen people and said city mobs add to government as sores do to the body, and agrarianism generally holds that farming builds virtue.

notes: Strands differ: Jeffersonian and Southern Agrarian traditionalism, agrarian socialism and Maoism, and centrist Nordic farmers' parties would answer economic and social questions quite differently. Jefferson and some Southern Agrarians tolerated slavery or segregation, which is not an agrarian doctrine as such.
